title: Business analysis and technology operation - Senior Manager
description:
**JOB DESCRIPTION**

**Sr. Manager – Technology Operations & Business Analysis**

LMS,Securitisation, BA, Regulatory Technology and IT Budget Control

**Designation** - Sr.Manager

**Department** - Technology & Operations

**Reports to** - Chief Technology Officer (dotted line to CFO, CBO)

**Team** - Individual contributor, in future team of 1–3 (business analysts, tech ops and MIS analysts)based on business growth; work with external vendors and system integrators

**Location** - Mumbai

**Experience** - 6-9 years in an NBFC/HFC, bank or fintech, with at least 3-4 years in a lead level role in technology programs, business analysis or operations

**1. Role Summary**

The AVP owns the interface between Treasury, Compliance, Finance and Technology. The role is accountable for the systems, data and controls that support securitisation, with priority on pass-through certificate (PTC) transactions, as well as direct assignment (DA), for translating RBI regulations into timely system and process changes, and for governing the technology budget so that spend stays aligned to business priorities.

The AVP leads a small team, represents Technology in senior management and committee forums, and is the single point of accountability for regulatory and securitisation data quality on the technology side. The role also carries technology-side ownership of data protection (DPDP Act) readiness and adherence to the company's IT governance framework.

**2. Key Responsibilities2.1 Securitisation and loan transfer (HFC) – PTC as priority**

* **PTC transactions (priority):** Own the technology and data readiness for pass-through certificate (PTC) issuances through an SPV/trust: pool cut, loan-level data tape, tranche-wise reporting and post-closing servicing, with faster and error-free turnaround on each deal.

* **Tranche structure:** Apply a working understanding of senior, mezzanine and junior (equity/first-loss) tranches, and of credit enhancement (overcollateralisation, excess spread, cash collateral, first-loss facility), when defining system logic, data fields and reports.

* **Cashflow waterfall:** Specify, build and validate the cashflow waterfall model: collections and prepayments, servicer and trustee fees, senior interest and principal, mezzanine and junior payouts, priority of payments, triggers and early-amortisation conditions, and reserve/escrow movements.

* **Reconciliation and controls:** Ensure each monthly waterfall run ties to servicer collections, escrow and trustee statements, and to tranche-wise investor payouts; investigate breaks and record sign-offs.

* Own the end-to-end technology and data framework for securitisation, DA and co-lending: pool selection, pool cut, loan-level data tapes from the LMS/LOS, and post-transfer servicing.

* Define and govern pool eligibility logic (seasoning, LTV, DPD, ticket size, ROI, product mix) against RBI norms, investor and rating agency criteria.

* Ensure system-level compliance with RBI's securitisation and transfer of loan exposures directions, including minimum holding period (MHP), minimum retention requirement (MRR), true-sale conditions and disclosures.

* Lead data and due-diligence support to Treasury, trustees, servicers, rating agencies, auditors and legal counsel; sign off on data integrity before submission.

* Drive automation of servicer and investor reporting, collection and escrow reconciliation, waterfall checks and pool performance MIS (collection efficiency, prepayments, delinquency).

* Ensure sold and reversed loans are correctly tagged in the core system, and that charge creation and satisfaction (CERSAI, ROC) and servicing flags remain consistent after transfer.

**2.2 RBI regulatory compliance (technology and data)**

* Run the regulatory change process: track RBI circulars and master directions for HFCs and NBFCs (scale-based regulation, IT governance, outsourcing of IT services, digital lending, KYC, fair practices, credit information reporting), assess impact and drive delivery to deadline.

* Own impact analysis, BRD/FRD approval, UAT governance and go-live sign-off for regulatory changes.

* Ensure the accuracy of regulatory returns and submissions through data mapping, source reconciliation, maker-checker controls and audit trails.

* Serve as the technology counterpart to Compliance, Risk and Internal/IS Audit; own closure of IT-related audit observations and report status to management.

* Support regulatory examinations and IT-related inspection queries with accurate, evidence-backed responses (see 2.6 for governance and data protection).

**2.3 IT budget control and vendor governance**

* Own the annual IT budget (CapEx/OpEx) across projects, vendors and cost centres; present budget-versus-actual and forecast to the CTO/COO and CFO monthly.

* Approve or challenge vendor invoices, SOWs, change requests and AMC/licence renewals against contracts and approved budgets.

* Lead business cases, TCO and ROI analysis for new initiatives; run the prioritisation of the change backlog with business heads.

* Flag overruns and forecast variances early and present corrective options; enforce spend discipline and approval workflows.

* Lead vendor negotiations, SLA reviews and contract renewals; maintain vendor scorecards.

**2.4 Technology operations**

* Govern the change request pipeline, release calendar, and incident and problem management for LMS, LOS, collections, treasury and finance systems.

* Set and track SLA and turnaround targets; ensure root-cause analysis and permanent fixes for repeat issues.

* Ensure process maps, data dictionaries, runbooks and SOPs are current and audit-ready.

* Oversee production support, reconciliations, and month-end and quarter-end closures with IT, operations and business teams.

**2.5 Team leadership and stakeholder management**

* Lead, coach and set objectives for the team; build depth in securitisation, regulatory and budgeting skills.

* Represent Technology in forums with senior management, auditors, rating agencies and, where required, RBI inspection and supervisory interactions.

* Build a risk and controls culture: documented ownership, segregation of duties and evidence retention.

**2.6 Data protection (DPDP) and IT governance**

* **DPDP Act readiness:** Lead the technology side of compliance with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and its Rules: data inventory and mapping across LOS, LMS, collections and vendor systems, consent and notice capture, purpose limitation, data principal rights (access, correction, erasure, grievance), retention and deletion, and personal data breach detection and reporting.

* **Data sharing in securitisation and vendor flows:** Ensure loan-level tapes shared with investors, trustees, rating agencies and vendors carry only necessary data, with masking or anonymisation where possible, and that data-processor contracts and access controls meet DPDP and RBI outsourcing requirements.

* **Governance framework:** Operate within RBI's IT governance, risk, controls and assurance requirements: maintain IT policies and their review cycle, prepare papers for the IT Strategy Committee, IT Steering Committee and Board, and track committee decisions to closure.

* **Three lines of defence:** Keep clear ownership, segregation of duties, access reviews and evidence retention for technology controls, and work with Risk, Compliance and Internal/IS Audit as first-line owner of remediation.

* **Third-party and resilience oversight:** Own IT vendor risk assessments, exit plans and BCP/DR test evidence, and review cyber incident reporting and information security controls with the CISO and Compliance.

* **Awareness:** Run periodic briefings for the team and business users on data handling, privacy and governance expectations.

**3. Required Qualifications and Experience**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Commerce, Finance or a related field; MBA (Finance), CA, CS or equivalent is a strong advantage.

* 10–14 years in an NBFC, HFC or bank, with hands-on exposure to securitisation, particularly PTC transactions, plus DA or co-lending operations.

* Strong understanding of securitisation structures: senior, mezzanine and junior tranches, credit enhancement, rating agency methodology and the cashflow waterfall, including the ability to build or review waterfall models in Excel/SQL.

* Deep working knowledge of RBI regulations for NBFCs/HFCs and how they translate into systems, data and controls.

* Working knowledge of the DPDP Act, 2023 and its Rules, and of RBI IT governance, outsourcing and cyber security requirements, with experience applying them in systems and vendor arrangements.

* Experience presenting to or preparing papers for IT/Board-level committees and handling audit or regulatory inspections.

* Proven experience owning IT budgets and vendor contracts, including variance management and business case approval.

* Strong SQL and Excel skills; experience with BI tools (Power BI, Tableau or similar); ability to review and challenge analyst work.

* Track record of delivering BRDs/FRDs, UAT and regulatory go-lives under fixed deadlines; familiarity with Agile and SDLC.

* Prior experience leading a team and presenting to senior management or committees.

**4. Preferred**

* Experience of end-to-end PTC issuance (arranger, trustee, rating agency and investor interactions) and of trustee/investor reporting platforms.

* Experience with LMS/LOS platforms used in housing finance, and with treasury tools.

* Understanding of housing loan products, LTV, PMAY subsidy processes and CERSAI/ROC filings.

* Familiarity with IS audit, ISO 27001 or COBIT, and API/integration basics.

* Certifications such as CBAP, PMP, CISA, CISM, CIPP/CIPM or Scrum, or data privacy certifications (e.g. DCPP).

**5. Key Competencies**

* Structured-finance thinking: comfort with tranching, credit enhancement and waterfall mechanics, and the ability to explain them to non-specialists.

* Strategic thinking with strong attention to data accuracy and control.

* Influence and communication with senior stakeholders, auditors and external counterparties.

* Prioritisation across regulatory, treasury and IT deadlines.

* Financial discipline and commercial judgement in vendor and budget decisions.

* Privacy and governance mindset: default to data minimisation, documented approvals and evidence.

* Ownership, integrity and people leadership in an audit-sensitive environment.

**6. Success Metrics (First 12 Months)**

* Zero data-quality exceptions in securitisation pool submissions and investor reports, with PTC deals executed on schedule.

* Tranche-wise waterfall reports reconciled to servicer, escrow and trustee statements every month with no unresolved breaks.

* All regulatory changes delivered on or before RBI deadlines.

* IT spend variance within the agreed tolerance of approved budget.

* Measurable reduction in change request turnaround time and in ageing of audit observations.

* DPDP data inventory, consent and breach-response process documented and approved, with gaps tracked to closure against the applicable timelines.

* IT governance committee papers and policy reviews delivered on schedule, with no overdue IT audit observations.

* Documented PTC data, waterfall and reporting framework, with automated reconciliations in place.

Pay: ₹1,800,000.00 - ₹2,200,000.00 per year

Work Location: In person

title: Information Technology Analyst
description:
At Dow, we believe in putting people first and we’re passionate about delivering integrity, respect and safety to our customers, our employees and the planet.

Our people are at the heart of our solutions. They reflect the communities we live in and the world where we do business. Their diversity is our strength. We’re a community of relentless problem solvers that offers the daily opportunity to contribute with your perspective, transform industries and shape the future. Our purpose is simple - to deliver a sustainable future for the world through science and collaboration. If you’re looking for a challenge and meaningful role, you’re in the right place.

**About you and this role**  
  
DOW has an opportunity for Information technology Analyst whose job will include a broad range of responsibilities in gathering and analyzing business requirements for assigned functional and technical areas. We also ensure that we operate on process operation, optimization, modification, maintenance, and technology implementation. We invite you to help us combine world-class expertise, future-focused technologies, and sustainability to solve global issues. You’ll work as part of a team at Dow, and we have many opportunities to address challenging real-world problems.  
  
**Responsibilities**

* Work on SAP Data Migration (Extract, Transform, and Load (ETL))
* Gathers and analyzes business requirements for assigned functional and technical areas.
* Works closely with business process teams, technical teams and other stakeholders to design and build objects which meet requirements.
* Document detailed designs.
* Builds, tests and implements application objects.
* Assists with issue resolution.
* Helps ensure that functional and technical designs meet business requirements, conform to Dow architecture standards, and optimize productivity and long-term product/system vision.

**Qualifications**

  

* Bachelor’s degree in IT discipline preferred.
* Minimum 3+ years of experience is required on the role.

**Your Skills**

* **Knowledge of SQL**
* **Knowledge of SAP Business Objects Data Services (BODS)**
* **Knowledge of Microsoft Power Apps**
* **Knowledge of PowerBI**
* **Good in communication and Analytical skills.**
* Knowledge of SAP Information Steward is a plus
* Knowledge of Material Master is a plus
* Knowledge of JAVA / JavaScript is preferred is a plus
* Knowledge of Data Quality concepts and trends is a plus
* Knowledge of Service Now workflow capabilities is a plus
* Good to have knowledge of Agile Methodology and Scrum Planning is a plus.

**Additional Notes**

  

* This position is available in Mumbai location.
* Relocation assistance is not available with this position..

**Benefits – What Dow offers you**

We invest in you.

Dow invests in total rewards programs to help you manage all aspects of you: your pay, your health, your life, your future, and your career. You bring your background, talent, and perspective to work every day. Dow rewards that commitment by investing in your total wellbeing.

Here are just a few highlights of what you would be offered as a Dow employee:

* Equitable and market-competitive base pay and bonus opportunity across our global markets, along with locally relevant incentives.
* Benefits and programs to support your physical, mental, financial, and social well-being, to help you get the care you need...when you need it.
* Competitive retirement program that may include company-provided benefits, savings opportunities, financial planning, and educational resources to help you achieve your long term financial-goals.
  + Employee stock purchase programs (availability varies depending on location).
* Student Debt Retirement Savings Match Program (U.S. only).
  + Dow will take the value of monthly student debt payments and apply them as if they are contributions to the Employees’ Savings Plan (401(k)), helping employees reach the Company match.
* Robust medical and life insurance packages that offer a variety of coverage options to meet your individual needs. Travel insurance is also available in certain countries/locations.
* Opportunities to learn and grow through training and mentoring, work experiences, community involvement and team building.
* Workplace culture empowering role-based flexibility to maximize personal productivity and balance personal needs.
* Competitive yearly vacation allowance.
* Paid time off for new parents (birthing and non-birthing, including adoptive and foster parents).
* Paid time off to care for family members who are sick or injured.
* Paid time off to support volunteering and Employee Resource Group’s (ERG) participation.
* Wellbeing Portal for all Dow employees, our one-stop shop to promote wellbeing, empowering employees to take ownership of their entire wellbeing journey.
* On-site fitness facilities to help stay healthy and active (availability varies depending on location).
* Employee discounts for online shopping, cinema tickets, gym memberships and more.
* Additionally, some of our locations might offer:
  + Transportation allowance (availability varies depending on location)
  + Meal subsidiaries/vouchers (availability varies depending on location)
  + Carbon-neutral transportation incentives e.g. bike to work (availability varies depending on location)

Join our team, we can make a difference together.

**About Dow Chemical International Pvt Ltd**

Dow Chemical International Private Limited (Dow India) aims to be the most innovative, sustainable, inclusive customer-centric materials science company. The company is committed to delivering the right solutions to its customers’ challenges. With broadest technology sets spanning performance materials, industrial intermediates, and plastics Dow India delivers differentiated science-based products and solutions in high-growth segments, such as packaging, infrastructure, automobile, and consumer care.

A Great Place to Work® Certified company with approximately over 1000 employees, its operations comprise of manufacturing sites, innovation center, established centers of excellence, and commercial office. As a responsible corporate, the company supports its Corporate Social Responsibility (program) with technology expertise and employee volunteerism. Dow India works with non-profit partners towards the empowerment of differently abled, women, and children in communities where it operates. The company aims to redefine the societal blueprint, by supporting holistic sustainability and circular economy initiatives.

As part of our dedication to inclusion, Dow is committed to equal opportunities in employment. We encourage every employee to bring their whole self to work each day to not only deliver more value, but also have a more fulfilling career. Further information regarding Dow's equal opportunities is available on www.dow.com.

title: AVP - Delivery Manager
description:
**About M&G India**

We are M&G India, the strategic innovation and digital hub for M&G. Established in 2003, we have offices in Mumbai and Pune.

Our teams work closely with colleagues across the Group worldwide to drive transformation, build digital capability, and support sustainable growth. By leveraging technology, AI, automation, and process excellence, we bring new ways of thinking to improve outcomes for both customers and colleagues.

Grounded in a vibrant culture with strong foundations, we are central to how M&G is transforming as a business.

**About M&G**

Our purpose is to give everyone real confidence to put their money to work. With a heritage dating back more than 175 years, we have a long history of innovation in savings and investments, combining asset management and insurance expertise to offer a wide range of solutions.

Our two distinct operating segments, Asset Management and Life, work together to provide access to balanced, long-term investment and savings solutions.

Through telling it like it is, owning it now, and moving it forward together with care and integrity; we are creating an exceptional place to work for exceptional talent.

• To work collaboratively with colleagues and take personal accountability to maintain and enhance controls you are responsible for to support improvement of the overall control environment, customers outcomes and a reduction in M&G plc's operational risk. • Own end-to-end delivery across assigned squad(s) or workstreams, from demand and initiation through planning, execution, release and closure, with clear accountability for delivery confidence, delivery health and outcome achievement. • Partner with Product Owners and business stakeholders to clarify outcomes, success measures, priorities, scope boundaries and acceptance expectations. • Build and maintain integrated delivery plans, release forecasts and milestones; communicate confidence, assumptions, options and trade-offs in business language, including the impact of delivery choices on cost, capacity, scope, risk and timelines. • Manage Scrum events including Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, Backlog Refinement, Sprint Review and Retrospective; ensure each sprint has a clear goal, realistic commitment and actionable improvement outcomes. • Coach teams in Scrum and Lean practices as appropriate, while protecting team self-organisation and avoiding command-and-control task allocation. • Ensure backlogs and work items meet the agreed Definition of Ready and Definition of Done, and that Jira data provides reliable traceability and delivery insight. • Actively manage RAID, cross-team dependencies, decisions, blockers, resource constraints and third-party commitments; escalate early with clear impact and recovery options. • Orchestrate delivery across squads, platforms and workstreams by managing decision flow, cross-squad dependencies, sequencing constraints and delivery assurance activities. • Use evidence and metrics such as predictability, throughput, cycle time, ageing work, escaped defects, release outcomes and team improvement trends to guide decisions. • Track delivery against intended benefits, measurable value, business outcomes and agreed success criteria, ensuring progress is visible beyond activity completion. • Coordinate release readiness across testing, architecture, security, risk, change, service management and application support, including operational handover, runbooks, monitoring, support contacts and known issues. • Maintain transparent stakeholder communication through concise status reporting, governance updates, demonstrations and decision forums, ensuring no surprises; own delivery input into senior governance forums, steering updates, escalation discussions and leadership reporting where required. • Promote quality, resilience, security, regulatory compliance and control adherence throughout the delivery lifecycle, including ownership of change-control readiness, audit evidence and regulatory delivery obligations where applicable. • Facilitate/participate in Scrum of Scrums or equivalent dependency forums where required and contribute to delivery standards, templates, communities of practice and continuous improvement, with focus on portfolio/workstream alignment, delivery risk visibility and consistent delivery assurance practices. • Create an inclusive, psychologically safe and accountable team environment where constructive challenge, learning and feedback are encouraged. • Mentor less experienced Scrum Masters and delivery colleagues and share reusable practices across the delivery community.

We have a diverse workforce and an inclusive culture at M&G Global Services, regardless of gender, ethnicity, age, sexual orientation, nationality, disability or long term condition, we are looking to attract, promote and retain exceptional people. We also welcome those who take part in military service and those returning from career breaks.
